messages:
incident-bot: Pager: smart-routing service degraded for multiple customers in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Priority: P1. On-call: jen
jen: acknowledging, jumping in. seeing elevated error-rate on requests routed to model-variant 'mixtra-v1-quant'.
jen: can someone grab the recent routing push? I think the config migration that landed ~2h ago touched the policy schema.
ryan: i merged the policy-schema change (schema-v2) at 15:12UTC — it was supposed to be backward compatible. i can pull the commit.
cory: putting logs here — repeated failovers between eu-west-1 and us-east-1, looks like auto-fallback triggers whenever model handshake returns 404-ish. logs snippet:
```
[2024-05-02T15:45:12Z] route_id=svc-1234 chosen_variant=mixtra-v2 status=OK
[2024-05-02T15:45:12Z] route_id=svc-1234 chosen_variant=mixtra-v1-quant status=deprecated_field_fallback
[2024-05-02T15:45:13Z] region=eu-west-1 fallback->us-east-1 reason=policy:auto_fallback
[2024-05-02T15:45:13Z] region=us-east-1 fallback->eu-west-1 reason=policy:auto_fallback
```
jen: those repeated back-and-forths = impact spikes and COLD cache misses. customers see latency + N responses.
maria: i've got a handful of customer reports — some SSO-based customers saw failed chats, others saw hallucinations. start triage: scope, rollback plan, comms.
jen: immediate plan: 1) stop the schema rollout (revert merge commit) 2) disable auto_fallback policy globally to break the loop 3) patch validator to reject deprecated fields that map to auto_fallback behavior
ryan: rollback CMD: `git revert --no-ff 9f3b2a4` then redeploy config service. initiating now.
cory: disabling auto-fallback flag across control plane: `curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/flags -d ' { "auto_fallback_enabled": false } '` — submitted, waiting for propagation.
deploy-bot: Rolling restart started for config-service (3 replicas), image config-service:v2024.5.2 -> v2024.5.3.
jen: good. monitor routing decisions after restart. can someone tail routing-metrics and kv-cache miss rate?
ryan: metrics: routing-fallback-rate spiked to 18% at 15:46UTC, now down to 4% after disabling flag. latency p95 for affected customers dropped from 1.8s -> 650ms.
maria: customer impact ETA: impacted customers ~22 (mostly EU SaaS customers). initial severity: degraded UX, no data exfil. recommending status page note: partial degradation for EU customers between 15:40-16:10UTC.
jen: root cause quick summary: schema-v2 introduced a renamed field `preferred_variant` -> `variant_preference` and a deprecated alias `auto_route` was interpreted as an on-by-default fallback policy by the control plane. That deprecated alias is set in some older team configs, so migrating to schema-v2 triggered implicit fallback semantics.
ryan: exact config that caused it (example from one customer policy):
```
# OLD customer policy snippet
route:
  model: mixtra
  preferred_variant: v2
  # legacy field, previously ignored
  auto_route: legacy_allow
```
jen: when schema-v2 accepted `auto_route` and coerced it to `auto_fallback: true` during migration, it unintentionally turned on auto-fallback for policies that were relying on the old silent-ignore behavior. that caused variants to be considered incompatible and triggered cross-region failovers.
cory: mitigation steps completed: reverted schema commit, restored config-service v2024.5.1, disabled global auto_fallback, added emergency config validator rule to block `auto_route` migration.
deploy-bot: Revert complete, config-service healthy.
jen: next steps: - run a small audit to find policies that include `auto_route` and contact owners - add a migration safety check to the control plane to require explicit accept of legacy semantics - update docs and notify partners - prepare PSAT/RC to reach out to impacted customers
maria: customer comms draft: "We briefly introduced a schema migration that unintentionally enabled a legacy routing alias, which caused increased latency and temporary misrouting for a subset of EU customers. No data loss. Full mitigation applied at 16:00UTC. We will follow up with root cause and timeline." thoughts? :thinking_face:
ryan: +1, add note about which model variants were affected (mixtra family) and that we reverted to previous routing behavior.
jen: assigning action items: ryan -> postmortem + migration safety check (ETA EOD). cory -> sweep and contact owners of policies with deprecated fields (ETA 4h). maria -> customer comms + status page (ETA 30m).
jen: also paging oncall handoff: i'm going offline in 45m, if anything flares escalate to cory.
aryan (typo): (ignore)
jen: closing notes: incident declared resolved at 16:00UTC after rollback and flag disable. will open a postmortem doc and link here. thanks everyone for fast responses. :heart:
